facts.fact: NewsDay reports that the Zimbabwe Republic Police's Horizon 2025 strategic plan decries manual management of information, which it says makes information hard to retrieve and leads to its loss and destruction; the plan is undated in the report, so the publication date is used.

The Information minister said after Cabinet on 14 December 2021 that a pilot study had been completed for digitising rural police stations under the Home Affairs ministry's integrated management system, with gadgets and connectivity still to be provided; no number of stations is given.

The report says the Zimbabwe Republic Police Horizon 2025 document, the force's five-year strategic plan, provides for Internet services for rural police officers to secure dockets, and Cabinet on 14 December 2021 announced the digitisation of rural stations to implement the ministry's integrated management system.
The Information minister on 14 December 2021 describes the integrated management system as the Home Affairs ministry's, with the rural station digitisation carried out through the regulator POTRAZ.
The Information minister said on 14 December 2021 that all costs of the digitisation would be borne by government, with each station's bandwidth subscription paid in full for 12 months.
